comment: Corporate-owned fully managed Android baseline. Public app installation and account changes are
blocked; approved Managed Google Play apps remain deployable by Intune.
2026-08-17: removed 'fingerprint' from passwordBlockKeyguardFeatures - it was blocking fingerprint
unlock at the keyguard entirely (this is what 'disabled itself' on the Moto G Stylus; it wasn't a
device bug, it was this policy). PIN/password was never blocked by this policy - passwordRequiredType
already requires numericComplex regardless of biometric state. 'face' stays blocked (not requested).
Also added playStoreMode: allowList so the Play Store itself only shows the curated app catalog,
further reducing exposure to Google's own apps/search beyond what googleAccountsBlocked already covers.
2026-08-17: flipped accountsBlockModification to false. It was blocking ALL account add/remove, which
would have also blocked adding a personal Microsoft Account for Microsoft Family Safety's lighter
parental controls. googleAccountsBlocked (still true, below) is the correctly-scoped restriction for
keeping Google accounts out specifically; it does not depend on accountsBlockModification being true.
2026-08-18: moved assignment from sg-tier-child to sg-devices-child because this is a corporate-owned
device restriction baseline and should target the dedicated child device group, not the user identity
tier group. Also set bluetoothBlockConfiguration to false per owner request and explicitly set
shareDeviceLocationDisabled to false so Intune admin Locate device capability remains allowed and the
config-as-code intent is documented rather than relying on the default.
name: android-fully-managed-restrictions-child

payload.description: Managed by sf-intune-cac. Do not edit in the portal.
